<thought>Based on the provided data, the molecule is most consistent with aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), which has the formula C9H8O4, 6 DBE, 6 aromatic carbons, 2 carbonyl groups, and 1 methyl group. The task asks to “link the fragments of the sample’s molecule and list their SMILES strings.” A logical way to split aspirin into two joinable fragments is:
1. The aromatic ring bearing the carboxylic acid (salicylic acid core): c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O
2. The acetyl group that is attached via an ester linkage: CC(=O)O

These two SMILES strings can be joined (through an ester bond) to reconstruct the full molecule. 

Thus the required answer is a list containing these two fragment SMILES. 
</thought>
<final_answer>['c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O', 'CC(=O)O']</final_answer>
